newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt police catch member of Sadat killing group.
newsitem.headline: Egypt police catch member of Sadat killing group.

text.p: Egyptian police have caught a militant Islamist who spent 16 years on the run after helping to found the group that assassinated Egyptian president Anwar Sadat, security sources said on Wednesday.
The militant, Hussein Ahmed Hussein, was sentenced in absentia to three years in jail in 1981 on charges related to the assassination, they said.
Police caught him in June and, in line with Egyptian practice in such cases, he went on trial for the same offences on Tuesday, they added.
Prosecutors say Hussein was a founding member of the fundamentalist Jihad group, members of which killed Sadat at a military parade on October 6, 1981.
The charges against him include taking part in attempts to Bchange the constitution, overthrow the government by force and assassinate government officials, the sources said.
They could not say how police captured him or where he had spent the last 16 years.
The trial adjourned until a second hearing on September 21.
